### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.completion

### Neovim version

0.11 (!at least latest Nightly build!)

### Description

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2c4556e-c5e5-4f42-817a-f88882a5f490

There is no auto-import when accepting a completion from an `lsp` that is configured to support snippets.

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

```lua
    
---@diagnostic disable: undefined-global
local function setup_deps(path_to_site)
  local mini_path = path_to_site .. "pack/deps/start/mini.nvim"
  if not vim.uv.fs_stat(mini_path) then
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    vim.fn.system({ "git", "clone", "--filter=blob:none", "https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim", mini_path })
    vim.cmd("packadd mini.nvim | helptags ALL")
    vim.cmd('echo "Installed `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
  end
  require("mini.deps").setup({ path = { package = path_to_site } })
end
setup_deps(vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/site/")

vim.g.mapleader = " "
MiniDeps.now(function()
  require("mini.icons").setup()
  MiniIcons.tweak_lsp_kind()

  MiniDeps.add({ source = "nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter", checkout = "master" })
  require("nvim-treesitter.configs").setup({ ensure_installed = { "rust" } })

  require("mini.snippets").setup() -- only using lsp snippets...
  require("mini.completion").setup({ lsp_completion = { auto_setup = false, source_func = "omnifunc" } })
  vim.opt.completeopt:append("fuzzy")

  MiniDeps.add("neovim/nvim-lspconfig")
  local snippetSupport = false -- without snippetSupport, auto-import works fine...
  require("lspconfig").rust_analyzer.setup({ -- have rust-analyzer installed...
    on_attach = function(client, buffer) vim.bo[buffer].omnifunc = "v:lua.MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp" end,
    capabilities = {
      textDocument = {
        completion = {
          completionItem = {
            snippetSupport = snippetSupport,
          },
        },
      },
    },
  })
end)
    
```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Interactive reproduction steps:
   
- Have [rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install) installed
- `cargo new demo`
- `cd demo`
- `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim src/main.rs`


```rust

fn main() {
    println!("Hello, world!");
}

struct Dog<Breed> {
    name: String,
}

```

-  Below name, type `breed: Phant` and accept completion item for `PhantomData`
- notice the auto-import at the top of the file
- in `init.lua`, set `snippetSupport = true`
- restart `nvim`, type again as described above: No auto-import.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

Unfortunately, I can not reproduce. The step " Below name, type `breed: Phant` and accept completion item for `PhantomData`" doesn't show any completion entries for me.

At the moment I suspect that this is an issue with 'rust-analyzer' not including `additionalTextEdits` in the response in the case of enabled snippet support. I also have the error at `Breed` while there is none in the issue's demo. Here is what it looks like:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9712391c-9d10-4d28-95ad-bc3f3b3607a1

---

Here is an example of a similar situation (auto-import when selecting snippet item) with Go and `gopls` where everything works as expected (although it required auto-importing `fmt` once by selecting its entry, undoing, and then selecting the suggested snippet entry) which shows that 'mini.completion' is capable of handling both snippet insert and auto-impor (i.e. `additionTextEdits`) at the same time:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b8994d4-a741-4653-9356-ac0700820016

This is with the following LSP-related part of the repro config:

<details><summary>Repro config for working `gopls`</summary>

```lua
	MiniDeps.add("neovim/nvim-lspconfig")
	local snippetSupport = true -- without snippetSupport, auto-import works fine...
	local capabilities = {
		textDocument = {
			completion = {
				completionItem = {
					snippetSupport = snippetSupport,
				},
			},
		},
	}
	require("lspconfig").rust_analyzer.setup({
		on_attach = function(client, buffer)
			vim.bo[buffer].omnifunc = "v:lua.MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp"
		end,
		capabilities = capabilities,
	})
	require("lspconfig").gopls.setup({
		on_attach = function(client, buffer)
			vim.bo[buffer].omnifunc = "v:lua.MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp"
		end,
		capabilities = capabilities,
	})

	-- Both `rust-analyzer` and `gopls` are installed with Mason
	MiniDeps.add("williamboman/mason.nvim")
	require("mason").setup()
```

</details>

---

Can you suggest other steps (either simpler or more detailed with Rust installation) that I can use to reproduce.
If that is difficult, could you examine the responses from 'rust-analyzer'? To do that, apply the following patch to the latest `main` of 'mini.completion', perform steps, and examine `_G.log` (it should contain both `additionalTextEdits` and `InsertTextFormat = 2` for the case which doesn't work):

```diff
diff --git a/lua/mini/completion.lua b/lua/mini/completion.lua
index 79f6fe3a..f66b0cbf 100644
--- a/lua/mini/completion.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/completion.lua
@@ -1030,6 +1030,7 @@ H.lsp_get_filterword = function(x) return x.filterText or x.label end
 H.lsp_item_compare = function(a, b) return (a.sortText or a.label) < (b.sortText or b.label) end
 
 -- Completion -----------------------------------------------------------------
+_G.log = {}
 H.make_completion_request = function()
   local current_id = H.completion.lsp.id + 1
   H.completion.lsp.id = current_id
@@ -1043,6 +1044,7 @@ H.make_completion_request = function()
   -- attached LSP client.
   local cancel_fun = vim.lsp.buf_request_all(buf_id, 'textDocument/completion', params, function(result)
     if not H.is_lsp_current(H.completion, current_id) then return end
+    table.insert(_G.log, result)
 
     H.completion.lsp.status = 'received'
     H.completion.lsp.result = result
@@ -1289,6 +1291,7 @@ H.info_window_lines = function(info_id)
   local cancel_fun = vim.lsp.buf_request_all(bufnr, 'completionItem/resolve', lsp_data.completion_item, function(result)
     -- Don't do anything if there is other LSP request in action
     if not H.is_lsp_current(H.info, current_id) then return end
+    table.insert(_G.log, result)
 
     H.info.lsp.status = 'received'
 
```

> At the moment I suspect that this is an issue with 'rust-analyzer' not including additionalTextEdits in the response in the case of enabled snippet support. I also have the error at Breed while there is none in the issue's demo. Here is what it looks like:

That error is in the demo as well. I don't know why, but diagnostics are only shown after a ":e" or an "edit and save", not when first opening the file.

Did you install rust on your local machine via the [link](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install) I supplied?

`curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh`

I don't think it works when `rust-analyzer` is installed through mason. You can install the `lsp` via `rustup`:

`rustup component add rust-analyzer`

Afterwards, you can remove rust from your system:

`rustup self uninstall`

I added the patch to the latest main and replayed the failing scenario. The output is huge, so it's in a temporary [repository](https://github.com/abeldekat/mini_issue_1721#)

> Did you install rust on your local machine via the [link](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install) I supplied?
> 
> `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh`

Sorry, no. I have it installed via `pacman` and I try to not execute (seemingly random) shell scripts from the Internet.

> I don't think it works when `rust-analyzer` is installed through mason.

This certainly explains my subpar experience with it when testing various 'mini.completion' new features 🤔 I'll take a closer look when/if I have time.

---

> I added the patch to the latest main and replayed the failing scenario. The output is huge, so it's in a temporary [repository](https://github.com/abeldekat/mini_issue_1721#)

Yes, it usually is. That's why there was this note about examining the actual request that contains completed data:

> ... and examine `_G.log` (it should contain both `additionalTextEdits` and `InsertTextFormat = 2` for the case which doesn't work): ...

Searching for `std::marker::PhantomData` showed 11 matches and none of the entries contains `additionalTextEdits` field, which is used for this kind of auto-import functionality. The most relevant log entry is probably [this one](https://github.com/abeldekat/mini_issue_1721/blob/cdfa12209a62b58ce5becfb6fe297a5d3a3069e0/output.txt#L6356-L6380) which shows the output of `'completionItem/resolve'` request.

Performing the same steps without snippet support (first part of the video) would probably show that the server response contains `additionalTextEdits` field. I would also assume that other completion engines behave the same here (i.e. no auto-import).

Judging by this data (even if I'd reproduced it locally), I'd conclude that this is not a 'mini.completion' but rather a `rust-analyzer` issue. If you happen to reproduce the "no auto-import while snippet support enabled" issue *with* the item containing `additionalTextEdits`, please add a comment.

Closing as (what very much looks like) a not 'mini.completion' issue.

>  I would also assume that other completion engines behave the same here (i.e. no auto-import).

I [checked](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/958a3997ce264e0e79faf78d63c4ebe7fb1b7905/lua/ak/deps/coding.lua#L9) that before creating the issue....) Both `nvim-cmp` and `blink` also add the import in the "with snippetSupport" scenario. The snippet is `PhantomData<%0>`.

> > I would also assume that other completion engines behave the same here (i.e. no auto-import).
> 
> I [checked](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/958a3997ce264e0e79faf78d63c4ebe7fb1b7905/lua/ak/deps/coding.lua#L9) that before creating the issue....) Both `nvim-cmp` and `blink` also add the import in the "with snippetSupport" scenario. The snippet is `PhantomData<%0>`.

Then maybe it requires manually setting more LSP client capabilities (as asked in [this comment](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1694#issuecomment-2749933263)). Could you try setting [all these capabilities](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/9d402c895aee27e053c765c65fbac4e5675db84d/lua/mini/completion.lua#L589-L627) instead of a single `textDocument.completion.completionItem.snippetSupport`?
I did so. Now I am not offered the `PhantomData` suggestion anymore...

> I did so. Now I am not offered the `PhantomData` suggestion anymore...

No completion items, no problems :)

I've finally managed to reproduce the whole issue locally. The absence of completion items seems to be due to absent `'additionalTextEdits` in `textDocument.completion.completionItem.resolveSupport.properties`. I.e. if it is absent, then `rust-analyzer` *for some reason* doesn't provide that completion candidate at all. Adding `'additionalTextEdits'` to resolve properties makes the completion item appear. I don't think this is a correct behavior of `rust-analyzer`, yet adding `'additionalTextEdits'` to that list in the future `get_lsp_capabilities()` seems like a more robust approach (as it follows what VS Code does and what evidently more servers support).

> The result: That response _does_ contain additionalTextEdits

After trial and error (and reproducing auto-import with built-in Neovim>=0.11 completion also), I've found the culprit. 'mini.completion' for items that need snippet insert uses [`label`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/687fa868d869078194c02065628712982d971fd6/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1108) as a `word` field. This means that when item is selected with `<C-n>`, `label` is inserted as text and LSP server resolves completion item with that text actually present in the buffer. For some reason `rust-analyzer` doesn't resolve completion item properly in this case.

So with this issue example:
- With `breed: ` already typed, type `Pha`. The item with `PhantomData<…>(use std::marker::PhantomData)` data should appear first and it needs a snippet insert. Now do one of the following:
    - Select with `<C-n>` - the full label is inserted in the buffer.
    - Select with `<Down>` - no new text is inserted in the buffer.
- Wait 100 ms until info window appears, press `<C-y>`. If selected with `<C-n>` - no auto-import; if with `<Down>` - auto-import. This is also reflected with present `additionalTextEdits` in the second case.

The reason it works for other completion engines is because they seem to insert `filterText` as text when navigating up/down. I don't necessarily agree with inserting part, but after reading and experimenting a bit I do agree that preferring `filterText` for `word` over `label` is better because built-in completion menu uses `word` to filter against the base. I thought it prefers `abbr` if it is present, but it seems to be wrong.

---

So:

- Not using `filterText` as `word` is a 'mini.completion' issue. I'll fix that.
- Not resolving completion item when there is some specific text in the buffer is an issue with `rust-analyzer`. I don't see anything about the guarantees about the text state in the LSP specification, so `rust-analyzer` should work with any text when processing `'completionItem/resolve'` request.
- Not providing completion items if `'additionalTextEdits'` is absent in resolve properties is an issue with `rust-analyzer`. I *guess* the logic here is "don't provide completion item if client can't support its *full* intentions (i.e. insert *and* auto-import)", but I'd guess that either providing `additionalTextEdits` right away or just not doing auto-import are more robust alternatives. That said, 'mini.completion' will list `'additionalTextEdits'` as one of resolve properties, but with a note about waiting for `delay.info` milliseconds.
- ~~This issue is the prime example of why I don't like working with LSP-related stuff~~

Did you install rust-analyzer with pacman? I am normally also hesitant to execute shell scripts from the internet. As an exception, I do trust the `rustup.rs` domain.

> ... Wait 100 ms until info window appears, press <C-y> ...

One of the parts I like about the current approach is not having to press `ctrl-y` for the snippet to activate. Any letter will do when the snippet has been selected with `ctrl-n`. Does this mean I have to remember to press `ctrl-y` in certain import-related cases?

> Tthis issue is the prime example of why I don't like working with LSP-related stuff

I understand that now...) Still, I am happy you found the problem as I very much like using `mini.completion`!

> Did you install rust-analyzer with pacman? I am normally also hesitant to execute shell scripts from the internet. As an exception, I do trust the `rustup.rs` domain.

I uninstalled `rust` installed with `pacman`, installed `rustup` with `pacman`, and then did everything with it, as it seems to be the most recommended approach. Had to figure out that adding '$HOME/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin' to the `PATH` manually is needed (but that is on me, as this is relatively obvious).

> One of the parts I like about the current approach is not having to press `ctrl-y` for the snippet to activate. Any letter will do when the snippet has been selected with `ctrl-n`. Does this mean I have to remember to press `ctrl-y` in certain import-related cases?

This (waiting for 100 ms) is the current behavior even with not pressing not :) It was a deliberate compromise to not have to deal with asynchronous completion item resolution and snippet expansion. As 100 ms plus server response is usually fast enough for users to select it and press any other key. This behavior will not change.

The `<C-y>` was used here because it is needed when choosing items with `<Down>` / `<Up>` (as they are not really *selected* as per built-in completion menu terms; thus no text is changed in the buffer). Pressing any key to accept the item (with all its snippet expansions and auto-imports) will remain to be the case if item was selected with `<C-n>` / `<C-p>` (and its `word` is put in the buffer).

And I am glad at least one other person like the "implicit accept" (with almost any non-keyword character) as opposed to "explicit accept" (after `<C-y>`), as I went several times back and fourth about whether this design is "too magical". But it seems to be very useful in practice at the (small-ish) cost to remember to explicitly stop completion with `<C-e>` if inserting an item is not needed.

The example in the first issue comment should now work on latest `main` (as `filterText` is now used over `label` for snippet items as a `word` field). Yet I still stand by the summary from [this comment](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1721#issuecomment-2772149589) in that there are two issues with `rust-analyzer` that can pop up in some other places.

Thanks! 

This fixes the issue, also *without* a call to `MiniCompletion.get_lsp_capabilities()`.

> ... also _without_ a call to `MiniCompletion.get_lsp_capabilities()`.

Yeah, because default capabilities and output of `get_lsp_capabilities()` are the same in fields relevant to this issue.

title: [mini.completion] No auto-import when lsp has snippet-support
